item.title: Steam will soon let users add hardware specs and performance data to reviews
item.description: According to the February 12 Steam beta patch notes, users can now automatically include hardware specs in game reviews and provide Valve with anonymized frame rate data. item.title: Automakers lose emissions credits for start-stop technology under new EPA rules
item.description: Start-stop is a relatively small feature with a dense engineering stack behind it. Modern systems tie together the engine control unit, starter-alternator hardware, beefed-up 12-volt or dual-battery architectures, and climate-control logic to shut the engine off during idle while keeping steering assist, brake boosting, and cabin comfort online.Read Entire Article

item.title: Driverless freight hits a new milestone with Aurora's 1,000-mile route
item.description: The journey takes Aurora's autonomous trucks roughly 15 hours, or about half the time a human operator could legally drive under federal hours-of-service rules. Existing regulations limit truck drivers to 11 hours of driving within a 14-hour window, require a 30-minute break after eight hours, and mandate a 10-hour rest...Read Entire Article

item.title: Researchers turn Edison's 1879 light bulb into a mini graphene reactor
item.description: Graphene is a two-dimensional lattice of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal pattern, renowned for its exceptional electrical conductivity, thermal transport, and mechanical strength. Turbostratic graphene is a stacked variant in which the layers are rotated and misaligned, weakening interlayer coupling and making the material easier to process at scale.Read Entire Article

item.title: Unreal Tournament 2004 is back – and it's free, with Epic's official blessing
item.description: One of PC gaming's greatest shooters has been given a free second life. Unreal Tournament 2004 is now available at no cost with Epic Games' blessing.
